location: Def physics:checker (line ~880: "$\sigma_\beta$ and $\omega_c$ are derived \emph{in the parent}"); Assumption physics:trusted (TB2); Thm physics:relative
problem: Def calculus defines ω_c semantically: {μ : λ[D:=μ]∈dom}∈𝒢 for λ∈‖ω_c‖. But the checker only requires ω_c to be derived in the parent, and (TB2) does not say ω comes from the catalogue. T3's (T2) said "with its well-posedness clause"; the paper drops even that. A solver can therefore cite ω_c := ⊤. Rope frame of Prop idealized(b) with the vacuously true "neglect rope mass" catalogue schema: the solver derives a=0 in the improper child (frame-valid steps plus ex falso), m_r ≤ η in the root, and ⊤ trivially. Every check passes, and the checker accepts |a| ≤ ε while |a| ≥ |Φ|/η. That is exactly the counterexample of Thm stipulation(c). So "All checks are deterministic" together with "for every solver whatsoever" is false as written. Round-2 re-verification flagged this ('provenance of omega_c'); it was not fixed.
proposed_fix: In Def checker, Schema indexing, replace "$\sigma_\beta$ and $\omega_c$ are derived \emph{in the parent}" with "$\sigma_\beta$ and the well-posedness certificate $\omega_\beta$ \emph{listed in the catalogue entry of $\beta$} are derived \emph{in the parent} (the solver may not choose $\omega_c$)". Append to (TB2): "each catalogue entry carries a well-posedness certificate $\omega_\beta$ for its declaration: for every $w$ and $\lambda\in\tset{\omega_\beta}_w$, $\{\mu:\lambda[D{:=}\mu]\in\dom\fM_w\}\in\fG$". In the proof idea of Thm relative add "(by (TB2), $\omega_c$ is a genuine certificate)".

location: Def physics:sps (line ~864); Thm physics:relative; paragraph "The residual \emph{judgment layer} is exactly (J1) ... (J2) ... (J3)" (line ~919)
problem: Def SPS makes ρ part of the solver's tuple: frame class, parameter roles, query and type, conventions, and hence Ax_ρ and W_ρ. The checker checks only that root axioms lie in Ax_ρ. Nothing checks that Ax_ρ holds on all of W_ρ, which Def frame(iii) assumes. A solver can declare the full α ∈ [30°,60°], so that (J1) W_ρ* ⊆ W_ρ holds, while placing α = 45° in Ax_ρ. The checker then accepts α-specific answers that are false at other completions. (TB1) also quantifies over the solver's W_ρ. So "exactly (J1)–(J3)" omits the judgment "ρ is a reading". The worked example escapes only because ρ is the trusted specification checked by C0. This was flagged in round-2 ('solver-supplied reading rho') and not fixed.
proposed_fix: In Def SPS replace "a reading $\rho$ (the frame class ...)" with "a reading $\rho$, which is the trusted problem specification or is checked against it: $W_\rho$, $Q$, its type and $\Ax_\rho$ must be those of the specification, or $\Ax_\rho$ must be kernel-derivable from the specification's axioms". Add to Def checker: "\emph{Reading:} $\rho$ is the trusted specification (or passes C0)". In the judgment-layer paragraph replace "(J1) \emph{reading containment}, $W_{\rho^*}\subseteq W_\rho$" with "(J1) \emph{reading adequacy}: $\rho$ is a reading ($\Ax_\rho$ holds at every $w\in W_\rho$) and $W_{\rho^*}\subseteq W_\rho$; when $\rho$ is the setter's formal specification only the second half remains".

location: Thm physics:nofree (c), line ~594: "$\mathcal C$ consists of restrictions of entire functions"
problem: Read as 𝒞 ⊆ {entire functions}, the claim is false: a singleton class admits an exact export rule. The proof needs Q + Aλ^{N+1} ∈ 𝒞, i.e. closure under adding polynomials, which T3 states as "the class of".
proposed_fix: Replace with "(c) $\mathcal C+\{\text{polynomials}\}\subseteq\mathcal C$ (e.g.\ $\mathcal C$ is the class of all restrictions of entire functions) and $I$ is the jet up to a finite order $N$".

location: Thm physics:judgment (b), line ~930
problem: The quantifiers are loose; round-2 flagged this. The counter-world must share the slice and the actual λ* the checker sees. "include worlds with actual μ*≠0" does not guarantee that.
proposed_fix: Replace "If the admissible extensions include worlds with actual $\mu^*\neq0$ and are closed under" with "If, for the given slice $\fM'(\cdot,0)$ and actual $\lambda^*$, some admissible extension has actual $\mu^*\neq0$, and the admissible extensions are closed under".

location: lines ~486–491, after Cor physics:blame: "with the root and the certified contexts as the \emph{only} designated contexts ... no false alarms while the reading is correct (T2 Thm~2.2)"
problem: Cor blame designates only certified contexts that have a properness witness. A certified but improper context can produce a false alarm even when the reading is correct. The reference also uses theory-file numbering instead of the paper's label.
proposed_fix: Replace with "with the designated contexts of \cref{cor:physics:blame} (the root, and certified contexts with properness witnesses) as the only designated contexts, an oligarchic-halving learner makes at most $\log_2(1/\wstar)$ detections and no false alarms while the reading and the certifications are correct (\cref{thm:coherence:halving}; false alarms are priced by \cref{thm:coherence:robust})".

location: Remark physics:existence, lines ~429–433

location: line 192: "Under limit semantics $\fF_c(w)$ is principal or improper"

location: Def physics:realization (R4), line ~358, and Thm physics:realizability(b)

location: start of sec:physics:export (line 567) and sec:physics:learning (line 739)
problem: Both subsections open with notation ('Fix a one-parameter deformation ...', 'A bridge schema $s$ has a dimensionless regime parameter ...') and never say what they establish.
proposed_fix: Insert at 567: 'Contexts let an idealized model contradict the world; exports carry its conclusions back. This subsection shows that no export is free: information about the idealized model alone, however complete (its jet, its germ, finitely many values elsewhere), never justifies a finite-tolerance claim at the actual parameter (\cref{thm:physics:nofree}). What justifies one is information of small radius about the de-idealized family (\cref{prop:physics:radius}), and we list the forms such certificates take. The subsection ends with the attack this creates: a solver who may choose contexts can stipulate any answer unless side conditions are evaluated in the parent and contexts are declared deformations (\cref{thm:physics:stipulation}).' Insert at 739: 'Export certificates need tolerances and validity regions, which are natural targets for learning. This subsection asks which signals learn them soundly against a solver who picks the regime. Coherence among exports catches only tolerances that are too narrow (\cref{thm:physics:coherencetol}); exchangeable calibration gives average coverage and nothing under selection; and only a \emph{proved} regularity property turns validated simulation of the top model into a sound certifier (\cref{thm:physics:lipschitz,thm:physics:monotone}).'
